Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: A higher Geriatric Depression Scale score was significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency in frail older hospitalized patients.
Sentence: "In a stepwise logistic regression analysis, only previous intake of vitamin D supplementation and high Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15) were significantly associated with vitamin D deficiency."
Measured as: Geriatric Depression Scale score (GDS-15)
Population: 217 consecutively admitted frail older geriatric hospitalized patients, mean age 81.6 years, 70% female
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D measured at hospital admission; no intervention given
Comparator: Not applicable (observational association; vitamin D sufficient vs deficient patients)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 217
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: UVB irradiation and oral vitamin D supplementation did not differ significantly in depressive symptoms in nursing home residents with dementia.
Sentence: "Intention-to-treat analysis with linear mixed modeling showed no significant between-group differences on agitation (p = 0.431) or depressive symptoms (p = 0.982)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (Cornell scale for depression in dementia)
Population: Nursing home residents with dementia
Intervention: Half-body UVB irradiation, 1 SED, twice weekly for 6 months
Comparator: Oral cholecalciferol 5600 IU once weekly
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 78
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
